description: morph morph is the IRCAM-era VOCINTE, written by Trevor Wishart during the composition of VOX-5. Morphs one PVOC spectrum into another, with amplitude and frequency interpolation start/end times controlled independently. This curated entry pins submode 1 (linear/exponential interpolation, shaped by expa/expf exponents); submode 2 (cosinusoidal spline) is uncurated.
musical_use: Smooth or staged crossfade between two timbres at the spectral level. Independent control of amplitude and frequency morphing lets you have one parameter lead the other — e.g. amplitude morphs early while frequency holds, then frequency catches up. Classic application: morph between two pitched sources, or between a pitched source and a noise-like one. Both inputs keep unfolding in time during the interpolation — each window of file 1 is interpolated with the simultaneous window of file 2 — so the morph rides two evolving sounds rather than two freezes. Best results come from sources that are already fairly similar; for distant timbres, pre-process one toward the other first (e.g. combine cross) for a more psycho-acoustically convincing transition.

expa.description: Exponent of amplitude interpolation (mode 1 only). 1 = linear; >1 = increasing slope; <1 = decreasing slope.

stagger.description: Time-delay of entry of the second file.

examples.description: Linear morph from file 1 to file 2 over the first 4 seconds, amplitude leading frequency by 1 second.
examples.expected_use: Spectral morph between two pitched sources where the timbre starts shifting before the pitch does.

known_issues: Differing-length inputs: use morph's own -s stagger flag (curated as the 'stagger' parameter); the engine does not pad or align input lengths.
